properties.statement: With the default error policy, an invalid one-based subscript on any selected axis of a rectangular gather faults, regardless of the storage contents or flattened offset.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} (dims : List Nat) (cells : List (Esm.Expr.Val α)) (subscripts : List Int), subscripts.length ≤ dims.length → (¬ List.Forall₂ (fun (n : Nat) (i : Int) => 1 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ (n : Int)) (dims.take subscripts.length) subscripts) → Esm.Expr.indexCell (.shaped dims cells) subscripts = .error .outOfRange

properties.statement: A gather whose base is a literal constant has the same result or error when the base is spelled as a name resolved to the identical constant value.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (name : String) (constant : Esm.Expr.Const) (args : List Esm.Expr.Ast) (value : Esm.Expr.Val α), Esm.Expr.constVal constant = .ok value → env.lookup name = some value → Esm.Expr.eval (.node "index" (.const constant :: args)) env = Esm.Expr.eval (.node "index" (.var name :: args)) env

properties.statement: A literal vector's one-based gather faults outside its extent.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} (cells : List α) (i : Int), (¬ (1 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ (cells.length : Int))) → Esm.Expr.indexVal (.arr1 cells) [i] = .error .outOfRange

properties.statement: An out-of-range subscript on either axis of a rectangular literal matrix raises the bounds fault.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} (rows : List (List α)) (width : Nat) (i j : Int), (∀ row ∈ rows, row.length = width) → (¬ ((1 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ (rows.length : Int)) ∧ (1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ (width : Int)))) → Esm.Expr.indexVal (.arr2 rows) [i, j] = .error .outOfRange

properties.statement: An out-of-range subscript on any axis of a rectangular rank-three literal raises the bounds fault.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} (planes : List (List (List α))) (height width : Nat) (i j k : Int), (∀ plane ∈ planes, plane.length = height ∧ ∀ row ∈ plane, row.length = width) → (¬ ((1 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ (planes.length : Int)) ∧ ((1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ (height : Int)) ∧ (1 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ (width : Int))))) → Esm.Expr.indexVal (.arr3 planes) [i, j, k] = .error .outOfRange

properties.statement: An unresolved variable raises the named fault in both whole-expression and per-cell evaluation.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (name : String) (ix : List Nat), env.lookup name = none → Esm.Expr.eval (.var name) env = .error (.unbound name) ∧ Esm.Expr.evalCell (.var name) env ix = .error (.unbound name)

properties.statement: If earlier strict operands evaluate successfully, an unbound variable in any remaining operand position aborts the expression with the corresponding named fault.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (op name : String) (strict : Esm.Expr.StrictOp) (before after : List Esm.Expr.Ast) (values : List (Esm.Expr.Val α)), Esm.Expr.Op.ofString op = .strict strict → Esm.Expr.evalList before env = .ok values → env.lookup name = none → Esm.Expr.eval (.node op (before ++ .var name :: after)) env = .error (.unbound name)

properties.statement: In a strict elementwise expression at a coordinate, the first unresolved variable after successful earlier operands faults with that name.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (op name : String) (strict : Esm.Expr.StrictOp) (before after : List Esm.Expr.Ast) (values : List (Esm.Expr.Val α)) (ix : List Nat), strict ≠ .index → Esm.Expr.Op.ofString op = .strict strict → Esm.Expr.evalCellList before env ix = .ok values → env.lookup name = none → Esm.Expr.evalCell (.node op (before ++ .var name :: after)) env ix = .error (.unbound name)

properties.statement: A resolved scalar operand contributes that scalar at every result coordinate.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (name : String) (value : α) (ix : List Nat), env.lookup name = some (.num value) → Esm.Expr.evalCell (.var name) env ix = .ok (.num value)

properties.statement: At a selected coordinate, strict elementwise evaluation applies the primitive to the recursively selected cells of its operands.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (op : String) (args : List Esm.Expr.Ast) (strict : Esm.Expr.StrictOp) (ix : List Nat), strict ≠ .index → Esm.Expr.Op.ofString op = .strict strict → Esm.Expr.evalCell (.node op args) env ix = ((args.mapM (fun arg => Esm.Expr.evalCell arg env ix)) >>= Esm.Expr.applyCell strict)

properties.statement: The checked gather of a materialized broadcast reads the result of applying the operation to that coordinate's broadcast operands.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} (apply : List (Esm.Expr.Val α) → Except Esm.Expr.EvalError (Esm.Expr.Val α)) (operands : List (Esm.Expr.ArrayData (Esm.Expr.Val α))) (result : Esm.Expr.ArrayData (Esm.Expr.Val α)) (ix : List Nat), Esm.Expr.ArrayData.broadcast apply .shapeMismatch operands = .ok result → List.Forall₂ (fun n i : Nat => i < n) result.dims ix → Esm.Expr.indexCell (.shaped result.dims result.cells) (Esm.Expr.oneBased ix) = Esm.Expr.ArrayData.broadcastCell apply .shapeMismatch operands ix

properties.statement: A complete gather of an elementwise expression with inferred extents returns the per-cell evaluator's result at the selected in-range coordinate.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (base : Esm.Expr.Ast) (args : List Esm.Expr.Ast) (dims ix : List Nat) (values : List (Esm.Expr.Val α)), Esm.Expr.isElementwiseGatherBase base = true → Esm.Expr.expressionDims base env = .ok (some dims) → dims ≠ [] → dims.length = args.length → Esm.Expr.evalList args env = .ok values → Esm.Expr.gatherSubscripts values = .ok (Esm.Expr.oneBased ix) → List.Forall₂ (fun n i : Nat => i < n) dims ix → Esm.Expr.eval (.node "index" (base :: args)) env = Esm.Expr.evalCell base env ix

properties.statement: A complete gather of an elementwise expression detects an out-of-range subscript on any axis before evaluating the selected cell.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (base : Esm.Expr.Ast) (args : List Esm.Expr.Ast) (dims : List Nat) (values : List (Esm.Expr.Val α)) (indices : List Int), Esm.Expr.isElementwiseGatherBase base = true → Esm.Expr.expressionDims base env = .ok (some dims) → dims ≠ [] → dims.length = args.length → Esm.Expr.evalList args env = .ok values → Esm.Expr.gatherSubscripts values = .ok indices → dims.length = indices.length → (¬ List.Forall₂ (fun (n : Nat) (i : Int) => 1 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ (n : Int)) dims indices) → Esm.Expr.eval (.node "index" (base :: args)) env = .error .outOfRange

properties.statement: After resolving a scalar condition, whole-expression ifelse evaluates only its selected branch, returning that branch's result or fault.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (condition yes no : Esm.Expr.Ast) (value : α), Esm.Expr.eval condition env = .ok (.num value) → Esm.Expr.eval (.node "ifelse" [condition, yes, no]) env = (if Esm.Expr.truthy value then Esm.Expr.eval yes env else Esm.Expr.eval no env)

properties.statement: After resolving the condition at a coordinate, per-cell ifelse evaluates and returns only the selected branch at that coordinate.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (condition yes no : Esm.Expr.Ast) (ix : List Nat) (value : α), Esm.Expr.evalCell condition env ix = .ok (.num value) → Esm.Expr.evalCell (.node "ifelse" [condition, yes, no]) env ix = (if Esm.Expr.truthy value then Esm.Expr.evalCell yes env ix else Esm.Expr.evalCell no env ix)

superseded_properties.statement: Gathering an in-range coordinate from a successfully evaluated elementwise array gives the primitive applied to that coordinate's broadcast operands.
superseded_properties.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [Esm.Closed.Scalar α] [Esm.Expr.Lits α] [Esm.Expr.Elem α] (env : Esm.Expr.Env α) (base : Esm.Expr.Ast) (args : List Esm.Expr.Ast) (values : List (Esm.Expr.Val α)) (op : Esm.Expr.StrictOp) (operands : List (Esm.Expr.ArrayData (Esm.Expr.Val α))) (result : Esm.Expr.ArrayData (Esm.Expr.Val α)) (ix : List Nat), Esm.Expr.ArrayData.broadcast (Esm.Expr.applyCell op) .shapeMismatch operands = .ok result → Esm.Expr.eval base env = .ok (.shaped result.dims result.cells) → Esm.Expr.evalList args env = .ok values → values.mapM (fun v => do Esm.Expr.asInt (← Esm.Expr.asNum v)) = .ok (Esm.Expr.oneBased ix) → List.Forall₂ (fun n i : Nat => i < n) result.dims ix → Esm.Expr.eval (.node "index" (base :: args)) env = Esm.Expr.ArrayData.broadcastCell (Esm.Expr.applyCell op) .shapeMismatch operands ix
superseded_properties.reason: Full elementwise gathers no longer materialize their base. The replacement laws separately cover committed array storage and selection through the elementwise AST, including when a different output cell would fault.
